text.p: The following are leading domestic stories in Portuguese newspapers.

- A partnership formed by EDP - Electricidade de Portugal, Transgas and Gas de Portugal, will operate in the telecommunications sector before the end of the year, competing with Portugal Telecom, Under-Secretary of State for Industry and Energy, Jose Penedos said.

- The Espirito Santo family banking group is trying to organize a core shareholder group, together with other foreign and domestic investors, to buy a controlling stake in Portugal Telecom during the company's third phase of privatisation, the paper said.
- Exports for most economic sectors, except the automobile sector, increased 3.9 percent during the last quarter.

- The leader of the opposition Social Democratic Party, Marcelo Rebelo de Sousa, said that he would not resign before parliamentary elections, due by 1999, and that he would be a candidate for prime minister.

- In 1996 15 percent of the active population was unemployed or under-employed and the highest unemployment rates were in Alentejo (13.8 percent) and Algarve (10.8 percent), according to the National Statistics Institute (INE).
- The Portuguese shoe-manufacturing industry will be the only one in the EU to grow and will invest mainly in the Spanish market, according to a study by a Spanish shoe sector association.
- The economy is expanding and all sectors are growing, according to INE's quarterly economic report. The same report says the economy will keep growing in 1997.

- Banco Comercial Portugues (BCP) sold 50 percent of its stake in the Colombo shopping centre, which is being built in Lisbon, to Dutch group International Neederlander Groep (ING). Colombo represented one of BCP's largest non-financial investments.
